claims.text: Applying a strong static magnetic field during solidification can increase the coercive field of magnetic high-entropy alloys.
A strong static magnetic field applied during solidification influences microstructure evolution, including phase species and phase volume fraction.
A strong static magnetic field applied during solidification influences atomic-level structure.
A strong static magnetic field applied during solidification influences defects, including vacancy and dislocation density.
Field-induced changes in microstructure, atomic-level structure, and defects alter magnetic properties, including coercivity.
The field-induced structural changes specifically cause an increase in coercive field.
Solidification under a 5 T static magnetic field will produce greater coercivity than solidification without a magnetic field.
The coercivity response depends on magnetic-field intensity and processing conditions.
The coercivity response may depend on the specific alloy composition.
The magnitude of any coercivity increase and the optimal field intensity may vary with alloy and processing conditions.
A matched experiment should compare samples solidified with and without a strong static magnetic field while measuring coercivity and structure.
Failure of the field-treated sample to show higher coercivity than the no-field control would falsify the directional hypothesis.
